answer: Seed the task river with honeypot jobs hiding a copper bounty behind a one-way canyon: trivial for any greedy policy to enter, effectively impossible for two independent minds to exit with the same trace. When a tide of near-identical solutions washes out of the same canyon, auditors burn the bonds of the whole correlated cluster. An attacker running N clones cannot send just one probe, because cloned policies share one greed: detection odds climb with N and a single catch slashes every correlated bond at once, so expected loss grows quadratically while pooled revenue stays linear.
